Verified defect: governance/transitions/T0090.json records timestamp 2026-08-25T01:40:00Z, which predates the Product-Owner authorization and the actual delivery by many hours. ... create T0091 recording that T0090's 01:40:00Z timestamp was erroneous and must not be used as evidence of authorization/execution chronology; preserve T0090 as historical evidence of the mistake; do not silently rewrite or backdate it.'
defect: T0090 records timestamp 2026-08-25T01:40:00Z. That is 8h45m BEFORE the commit that introduced it (6cd889c, authored 2026-08-25T10:25:22Z) and 8h41m BEFORE the Product-Owner authorization that requested the work (2026-08-25T10:21:45Z). The receipt therefore claims a moment at which neither the authorization nor the work existed.
why_it_happened: The timestamp was chosen by hand as a plausible-looking round time instead of being derived from the commit clock. Governance rule 1d only forbids a receipt dated AFTER its introducing commit, so a timestamp far too EARLY passes every automated check while still being false. The same hand-picking produced the opposite error in T0087 and T0088, where the invented time landed after the commit and the validator caught it. T0091's timestamp is derived from git, not chosen.

verified_chronology.source: git log on the merged commits and the GitHub pulls API for #46. Every value above is read from a durable record, none is estimated.

evidentiary_status_of_t0090: T0090's substantive content - the corrected Room sign-in wording it receipts - remains VALID and in force. ONLY its timestamp is erroneous. T0090's 2026-08-25T01:40:00Z MUST NOT be used as evidence of when authorization was given or when execution occurred. For that, use the verified chronology above.
preservation: T0090 is PRESERVED UNCHANGED as historical evidence of the mistake. It was deliberately not rewritten, not backdated and not deleted: a corrected record that hides the error teaches nothing and cannot be audited. This correction is append-only.
